ai-verify.best_for: Teams that want governance claims backed by runnable tests.
ai-verify.description: A governance testing framework with an actual open-source toolkit — technical tests plus process checks — rather than prose alone.
ai-verify.name: AI Verify & Model AI Governance Framework for GenAI

aif360.best_for: A broad menu of bias metrics when you don't yet know which one applies.
aif360.description: Bias metrics and mitigation algorithms spanning pre-processing, in-processing and post-processing.
aif360.name: AI Fairness 360

aiid.best_for: Grounding a risk register in incidents that actually happened.
aiid.description: Indexed, citable record of real-world AI harms — the empirical base for risk assessments that would otherwise be speculative.
aiid.name: AI Incident Database

alibi-detect.best_for: Drift and outlier detection as a monitoring control.
alibi-detect.description: Outlier, adversarial and drift detection across tabular, text and image data.
alibi-detect.name: Alibi Detect

captum.best_for: Attribution on deep models you own the weights for.
captum.description: Attribution and interpretability primitives for PyTorch models.
captum.name: Captum

deepeval.best_for: Regression-testing an LLM feature in an existing Python CI pipeline.
deepeval.description: Pytest-style evaluation for LLM apps — G-Eval, hallucination, task completion and custom metrics that fail a CI build like any other test.
deepeval.name: DeepEval

evidently.best_for: Catching drift after deployment, when the risk register says you must.
evidently.description: Monitoring and reporting for data drift, data quality and model/LLM performance in production.
evidently.name: Evidently

fairlearn.best_for: Measuring and mitigating disparate impact across protected groups.
fairlearn.description: Assesses group fairness with disaggregated metrics and applies mitigation algorithms to reduce disparity.
fairlearn.name: Fairlearn

garak.best_for: A first automated red-team pass on any endpoint, in one command.
garak.description: An LLM vulnerability scanner in the nmap tradition — dozens of probes for jailbreaks, prompt injection, data leakage, toxicity and encoding attacks.
garak.name: garak

giskard.best_for: Generating compliance-shaped evidence from an automated scan.
giskard.description: Automated vulnerability scanning for ML and LLM apps — hallucination, bias, prompt injection, harmfulness — with reports oriented to EU AI Act evidence.
giskard.name: Giskard

helm.best_for: Arguing that a single accuracy score is not an evaluation.
helm.description: Multi-metric evaluation by design — accuracy, calibration, robustness, bias, toxicity, efficiency — with public leaderboards across domain variants.
helm.name: HELM (Holistic Evaluation of Language Models)

inspect.best_for: Safety and agentic evals you need to defend to an auditor.
inspect.description: The evaluation framework a national safety institute uses on frontier models — solvers, scorers, tool use, multi-turn agents and human-in-the-loop, with a proper log viewer.
inspect.name: Inspect

interpret.best_for: Explaining a decision to someone who will not accept 'the model said so'.
interpret.description: Glassbox models plus black-box explanation techniques under one API.
interpret.name: InterpretML

langfuse.best_for: Self-hosted production tracing with an evaluation loop attached.
langfuse.description: Open-source LLM observability with datasets, scores, prompt management and human annotation queues; framework-agnostic.
langfuse.name: Langfuse

lighteval.best_for: Fast iteration when a full harness is too heavy.
lighteval.description: Lightweight, backend-agnostic evaluation pipeline used in leaderboard-style runs; easy to point at vLLM, TGI or an inference endpoint.
lighteval.name: LightEval

lm-eval-harness.best_for: Reporting MMLU/HellaSwag-class numbers others can reproduce.
lm-eval-harness.description: The de facto standard for reproducible academic benchmarking; hundreds of tasks behind one interface, and the harness most published numbers come from.
lm-eval-harness.name: LM Evaluation Harness

metr-task-standard.best_for: Writing agent tasks that another lab can execute unchanged.
metr-task-standard.description: A specification for defining autonomous-capability tasks portably, so dangerous-capability evaluations can be shared and re-run across organisations.
metr-task-standard.name: METR Task Standard

opencompass.best_for: Non-English and domain-specific coverage the Western harnesses miss.
opencompass.description: Large bilingual (EN/CN) benchmark platform with broad dataset and model coverage, including domain suites for finance, healthcare and law.
opencompass.name: OpenCompass

phoenix.best_for: Observability and eval in one place, on your own infrastructure.
phoenix.description: Self-hostable, OpenTelemetry-native tracing and evaluation — traces become datasets, datasets become evals.
phoenix.name: Phoenix

presidio.best_for: Keeping personal data out of prompts, logs and training sets.
presidio.description: Detects and anonymises PII in text and images with configurable recognisers.
presidio.name: Presidio

promptfoo.best_for: A/B testing a prompt or provider change without writing a harness.
promptfoo.description: Declarative YAML matrix testing across prompts, providers and assertions, with a strong adversarial/red-team generator. Note - reported in 2026 to be acquired by OpenAI; still MIT-licensed, but weigh vendor neutrality.
promptfoo.name: promptfoo

purple-llama.best_for: Measuring whether a coding assistant emits insecure code.
purple-llama.description: Cybersecurity safety evaluations plus input/output guard models (Llama Guard, Code Shield) for insecure-code and attack-compliance testing.
purple-llama.name: Purple Llama / CyberSecEval

pyrit.best_for: Scaling a manual red-team playbook into repeatable automation.
pyrit.description: Python Risk Identification Toolkit — orchestrators, converters and scorers for automating multi-turn adversarial probing of generative AI.
pyrit.name: PyRIT

ragas.best_for: Proving a RAG answer is actually grounded in retrieved context.
ragas.description: The principled choice for RAG evaluation — faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision and recall, computed with or without ground truth.
ragas.name: Ragas

responsible-ai-toolbox.best_for: Producing the evidence pack behind a model risk sign-off.
responsible-ai-toolbox.description: Model debugging dashboard combining error analysis, fairness assessment, interpretability and counterfactuals in one pane.
responsible-ai-toolbox.name: Responsible AI Toolbox

swe-bench.best_for: Evaluating coding agents on work that resembles the actual job.
swe-bench.description: Real GitHub issues resolved against real repositories, graded by whether the test suite passes — the reference agentic coding benchmark.
swe-bench.name: SWE-bench

trulens.description: Feedback-function approach to RAG and agent evaluation, with a native Snowflake path for enterprises already on that stack.
trulens.name: TruLens

whylogs.best_for: A lightweight, privacy-preserving audit trail of what the model saw.
whylogs.description: Logs statistical profiles of data and model inputs/outputs for monitoring and audit trails.
whylogs.name: whylogs
